parts.label: (i)
parts.answer: $x=\frac2k$ is a maximum and $x=\frac4k$ is a minimum.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Attempt differentiation and set equal to zero: $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{k}{(kx-3)^2}+k=0$ (***M1**; must contain $(kx-3)^{-2}$ and other term). Simplify to a quadratic/equivalent: $(kx-3)^2=1$, or $k^2x^2-6kx+8=0$ (**DM1**). Obtain $x=\frac2k$ and $x=\frac4k$ (***A1 *A1**, legitimately obtained). $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\frac{2k^2}{(kx-3)^3}$ (**B1**, follow-through must contain $Ak^2/(kx-3)^3$ where $A>0$). At $x=\frac2k$, second derivative is negative: maximum (**DB1**); at $x=\frac4k$, second derivative is positive: minimum (**DB1**; convincing alternate methods must show which values are used and cannot use $x=3/k$).

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: $V=\pi\int_0^2[(x-3)^{-1}+(x-3)]^2\,dx$ (***M1**; attempt to expand $y^2$ and integrate). Expand to $(x-3)^{-2}+(x-3)^2+2$ (**A1**). Integrate to $[-(x-3)^{-1}+\frac{(x-3)^3}{3}+2x]_0^2$ (**A1**; condone missing $2x$). Apply limits $0\to2$ (**DM1**). $V=\frac{40\pi}{3}$ or $41.9$ (**A1**; missing $2x$ gives $28\pi/3$, scoring $M1A0A1M1A0$).
